answer: An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Because the summit index resolves every citation against the island checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the echo audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 84 aliases as a result pays the authoring cost 84 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 29 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
